qt: to the Commission Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR) Subject:

According to a complaint lodged on 29 October 2026 by the Panhellenic Association of Employees of the Organisation for Employment of the Workforce (OAED), previously the Workers’ Housing Organisation (OEK), Greece has spent more than EUR 5.2 million on surveys, monitoring and the administrative planning of housing policy.1 Specifically, the complaint mentions EUR 543 120 for the National Housing Policy Strategy, EUR 1.46 million for a mechanism for monitoring housing precariousness and almost EUR 3 million for the preparation and initial operation of a new Single Housing Policy Body. The National Strategy was financed by the Recovery Fund and the Commission often points to the severe shortage of social housing in Greece. At the same time, the Panhellenic Association of Employees of the Organisation for Employment calls for transparency on the reserves of the former Workers’ Housing Organisation, which the association claims exceed EUR 1.2 billion, and for existing public know-how to be used instead of permanent recourse to external consultants. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Which of the above expenditure is financed by EU resources, in particular through the Recovery Fund and the NSRF, which amounts have already been disbursed and which specific deliverables have been completed?
Has it assessed the necessity and cost-effectiveness of advisory services, in particular against the use of existing public structures?

What specific, measurable objectives for the construction or provision of social housing are linked to European-funded interventions and how is it ensured that resources deliver tangible results for citizens facing housing precariousness?
